label: 234 eastex identity
definition: ercot-234 KEEPER (card Z-A identity repair, owner-signed 2026-08-25): EASTEX — ERCOT's East Texas GTC, the constraint that physically exists at the model's Northeast->North boundary — replaces the geographically mis-attributed NE_LOB (North Edinburg-Lobo, a Rio Grande Valley corridor read as 'Northeast lobe' since the zone was built) in the measured-GTC crosswalk; static export rating re-derived 1,300 -> 2,300 MW (NP6-86 mean-limit-at-bind 2023+2024). Zero fitted scalars. All P-6 gates PASS: no new shed, coal rise <= 0.21 TWh, G-SPUR 2023 21 -> 11 (the ercot-231 promotion's named cost dissolves), NE|N separation 2,155/1,128/1,354 -> 29/45/45 h (the real EASTEX scale). Officials: 2023 -39.7% / 0.730 / C3c 72 (the mis-attributed gain returned per rule 14), 2024 -0.2% / 0.131 / 22, 2025 -7.9% / 0.101 / 1; NOT-YET on {C3a-2023, C3b-2023}, C3c ledgered x3.
market_story: Northeast (East Texas) lobe: ~8 GW of coal+gas behind ERCOT's EASTEX voltage-stability export interface serves ~3.5% of load; the real market congests this boundary rarely (EASTEX bound ~69/16/<1 h-equivalents 2023-2025 at a ~2.3-2.4 GW limit, effectively unconstrained by 2025 after VSAT-based GTLs) — so Martin Lake / Welsh / the NE CCs clear at near-system prices almost every hour, and the model now reproduces that (29/45/45 separated hours) instead of manufacturing 1,100-2,200 congested hours from the Rio Grande Valley's NE_LOB series. The Valley corridors (NE_LOB, VALEXP, NELRIO, RV_RH) are intra-South pockets this 7-zone topology cannot represent and are excluded from the crosswalk rather than mis-placed. Tie-zone interchange attribution (ercot-231) stays armed: measured EIA-930 per-neighbor DC-tie flows at the tie-host zones (Monticello DC-East in Northeast, Oklaunion in North, Mexico ties in South).
